summary: Ryosaburo Sakaki was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He taught at Ryukoku University, the Third Higher School, and as a professor at Kyoto University from 1908.

Ryosei Fukuda specialized in Buddhist studies, completing his education and doctorate at Toyo University. He became a professor at Taisho University in 1973 and emeritus in 2007, later holding leadership posts at Chisan institutions and Shuchiin University.

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He served as a professor at Hanazono University from around 1987 to 2018, later becoming emeritus, and held research posts at Soto Zen institutes.

Ryosho Hayashi worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology, studying at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He spent his career at Taisho University, becoming a professor in 1975, dean of literature in 1981, and president from 1990 to 1994.

Ryosho Nakamura is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Seventh Higher School, Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, and Rissho University. He served as a professor at Kagoshima International University from around 1968 to 1998.

Ryosho Tanaka was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University. He served Komazawa as a professor from 1964, dean, museum director, and president in 2009, and was also a professor at Ryukoku University.

Ryoshu Kouda works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Seitatsu Matsunami and held researcher appointments at Taisho University in 1998 and the Hasegawa Buddhist Cultural Institute in 2006.

Ryoshu Michihata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University, where he later taught from around 1947 to 1967, and served as a professor at Kyoto Koka Women's University from around 1967 to 1980.
Ryoshu Misaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from around 1947 to 1952. He spent his career there from around 1958 to 1992, becoming an emeritus professor.

Ryoshun Okubo specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Waseda University, he became Professor of Sino-Japanese Buddhism there around 1993, while also holding posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.
Ryosuke Furui is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and holds a professorship at the University of Tokyo.

Ryota Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies and served as a graduate researcher at Toyo University in 2015. In the same year, he held a research post at the Shinran Buddhist Center.
Ryotai Shibuya was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed studies at Tendai Sect University and Kokugakuin University.
Ryoun Yamada is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Harvard Business School. After a banking and corporate career from 1964 to 2000, he became the leader of Sanbo Zen in 2004.

Ryudo Fujii works in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Albrecht Wezler and Harunaga Isaacson, held a JSPS research fellowship in 2003, and lectured at Kokushikan University and Kyoto Women's University.
Ryudo Suita is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer and held an academic post at Bukkyo University between 1997 and 2020.

Ryugen Taga is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He spent his career at Rissho University as a lecturer, associate professor, professor from around 1975 to 2002, and president from around 1992 to 1995.

Ryugen Tanemura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held teaching posts at Nishogakusha University and Taisho University, as well as a research position at Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.

Ryuichi Abe works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Educated at Keio, Johns Hopkins, and Columbia under Yoshito S. Hakeda and Philip Boas Yampolsky, he taught at Columbia before becoming Reischauer Institute Professor of Japanese Religions at Harvard.

Ryujo Yamada was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He served as a professor and emeritus professor at Tohoku University, as head of Musashino University, and contributed to Hōbōgirin.
